There are a number of ways to explain this:

1) the word "for" is a preposition, so it is always followed by an object form : me, us, them, etc . In this case "ME" is the object form of the first person singular. Thus "for ME" "for HIM.

Similarly, we say "between you and ME" - because "between" is a preposition and thus always introduces an object. So we do not say "between you and I".

2) The basic English clause is formed Subject + Verb + Object. Someone does something to something.

I (subject) went (verb) to the gas station (Indirect Object) for (preposition) my gf and ME (direct object).

Again, object forms of the pronouns are "me, us, them, him, her, etc,
